\sigmainn \colon \wDomainOneD \to \wDomainRPOneD$ is invertible with $\sigmainn'(z)=0$ if and only if $z \in \partial \wDomainOneD$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption (A2) only requires sigmainn to be C^1 with sigmainn' vanishing on the boundary of wDomainOneD. Then h'(z) = ([sigmainn^{-1}]'(z))^2 = sigmainn'(sigmainn^{-1}(z))^{-2} blows up at the boundary, so the right-hand side of the reparametrized ODE is merely continuous, not locally Lipschitz, there; the Picard-Lindelöf uniqueness argument in the proof of (i) is therefore invalid (continuity does not imply local Lipschitz continuity), and trajectories can reach ∂wDomainRP in finite time whenever ∫ dwprod / sigmainn'(sigmainn^{-1}(wprod))^2 < ∞ at the boundary. This happens for the polynomial reparametrization sigmainn(z) = |z|^{2/p} with p ∈ (1,2) (time-to-hit ∫ wprod^{p-2} dwprod < ∞ iff p > 1). Concrete counterexample satisfying (A1)-(A3) and (B2): p = 3/2, A = [[1,1,0],[0,1,1]], y = (1,1), wprod_0 = (0.01,5,5). Then wprod_1 reaches 0 in finite time and stays there (sigmainn'(0)=0), the flow on the face {wprod_1 = 0} converges to (0,1,0), but the Bregman objective <bo, H(z) - z⊙h(wprod_0)> over {z ≥ 0, Az = y} is minimized at the interior point ≈ (0.237, 0.763, 0.237), not at (0,1,0). Hence (i) is false, and the conclusion of (ii) fails although all its hypotheses hold (the limit exists, LossM = 0, and h, H are finite at the boundary for p > 1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption (A2) with a boundary regularity condition that makes the time to reach ∂wDomainRP infinite (e.g. require sigmainn' to be Lipschitz on wDomainOneD, equivalently ∫ dwprod / sigmainn'(sigmainn^{-1}(wprod))^2 = ∞ at the boundary). This necessarily excludes the polynomial reparametrizations with p ∈ (1,2); no repair preserves the conclusion for p ∈ (1,2) because the limit itself need not be the Bregman minimizer.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central implicit-bias theorem loses both its trajectory-interior claim (i) and its Bregman characterization (ii) precisely in the advertised ℓ_p-interpolation regime p ∈ (1,2). Every result justified via Theorem vector_IRERM (i)/(ii) or via the preamble of Theorem thm:Convergence (which cites (i) to keep wprod in int(wDomainRP), e.g. for the chain rule in lem:decay) becomes unreliable for p ∈ (1,2), including the polynomial regularization corollaries and the showcase theorem thm:PolynomialRegularizationIntroduction in that regime.
issues.title: Trajectories can reach the boundary of wDomainRP in finite time; the implicit-bias theorem is false as stated
issues.why_classification: The main theorem is false as stated (not merely unproved) in a concrete instance satisfying all assumptions, and the failure occurs in the paper's advertised p ∈ (1,2) interpolation regime; every supported repair adds a hypothesis that withdraws that regime, which is a major loss of scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The decay estimate ∂_t D_F(z̃_0, wprod(t)) ≤ -LossM(wprod(t)) is derived from the first-order convexity inequality <∇L(v), v' - v> ≤ L(v') - L(v), but convexity of L(·,y) is not part of (A3) (nor of (B1),(A2),(A3),(B2)). Without it the lemma and the convergence theorem are false: for the (A3)-compliant loss L(v,0) = (1/2)||v||^2 e^{-||v||^2} with sigmainn = Id, A = 1, y = 0, w_0 = 1, the flow w' = -w(1-w^2)e^{-w^2} escapes to +∞ with LossM(w(t)) ~ sqrt(log t)/(4t), violating the claimed O(1/t) rate; and z·h'(z) = z lies in F_D, yet sup_t ||w(t)|| = ∞, contradicting the boundedness conclusion of thm:Convergence (iii).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add convexity of L(·,y) to the assumptions of lem:decay and Theorem thm:Convergence. Then the decay inequality and the O(1/t) rate hold, and - because convexity together with the unique-minimizer condition forces sublevel sets to be bounded - the claim lim A wprod(t) = y also follows; no rate or guarantee is lost for convex losses (all applications).
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rates and the boundedness criterion in Theorem thm:Convergence, and hence the existence-of-limit claims in both showcase theorems and their convergence corollaries, are unsupported for general (non-convex) losses; the stated O(1/t) rate itself is false for a concrete loss satisfying (A3).
issues.title: The O(1/t) rate and the boundedness criterion require convexity of L(·,y), which is nowhere assumed
issues.why_classification: The stated theorem is false without the missing hypothesis (a concrete counterexample violates the rate), so a repair is required; but the repair is a contained hypothesis addition (convexity, already tacitly assumed in the paper's own prose) that leaves all rates and applications intact - more than minor, yet no new proof architecture and no major loss.
